residual_risks: django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:~34 calls user.get_session_auth_fallback_hash() on any hash mismatch. A custom user object that defines get_session_auth_hash (so passes the hasattr gate) but does not subclass AbstractBaseUser would raise AttributeError (HTTP 500) on a stale session instead of flushing it. This fails closed (no authentication bypass) but is a behavior regression for duck-typed user models.

AbstractBaseUser subclasses that override get_session_auth_hash will not get fallback-secret support, because get_session_auth_fallback_hash is built on the private _get_session_auth_hash. Their sessions are flushed on rotation (fail closed), not accepted. Documented-behavior gap, not a vulnerability.

Fallback acceptance is by design: any secret left in SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS remains able to validate session hashes until it is removed. A compromised retired key stays useful to forge sessions while listed, but this is inherent to the feature.
testing_gaps: No test that a session hash matching neither the current secret nor any fallback is still flushed when SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS is non-empty.
No test that a missing or empty session hash still flushes with fallbacks configured.
